Chapter:
Installation and Preface
To install the package, just unpack it in your packages directory (usually ~/gap/pkg for local installation).
To use polymaking, you need a working installation of the program polymake https://polymake.org. The package has been tested on linux and Mac OS X (10.4, 10.5 and 10.6). But it should be as platform independent as &GAP; and polymake.
The interaction with polymake is restricted to writing files and carrying out simple operations. polymaking writes a data file in polymake's own JSON format and then asks polymake to evaluate properties of it, using the script lib/pm.pl:
polymake ––script lib/pm.pl RESULTFILE OBJECTFILE KEYWORD1 KEYWORD2
The keywords are polymake properties or methods without arguments. The script writes the results as JSON to RESULTFILE, which &GAP; reads back with the json package; going through a file rather than through standard output keeps the results clear of anything polymake prints.
Using custom scripts is not supported.
Every call to polymake will re-start the program anew. This causes considerable overhead. The number of calls to polymake is reduced by caching the results in the so-called PolymakeObject in GAP. As of polymaking version 0.9.0, polymake 4.0 or newer is required. Use polymaking 0.8.9 with older versions of polymake.
A few words about the installation of polymake
polymaking looks for a program named polymake in your PATH every time it calls polymake. If this fails, a warning is issued at load time (InfoWarning level 1) and you have to say where polymake lives, see .
setenv PATH ${PATH}:<your polymakepath>
The general rule is: If polymaking finds polymake by itself, there is nothing to worry about.
Configuring polymaking
polymaking is configured through the &GAP; user preference mechanism (see ). Two preferences are available, both empty by default:
PolymakeCommand
the command or path used to invoke polymake. Empty means: look for polymake in DirectoriesSystemPrograms(). PolymakeDataDirectory
the directory in which the files handed to polymake are created. Empty means: use a temporary directory, created on demand and removed when &GAP; exits. PolymakeQuiet
whether to suppress polymake's informational messages, such as the credits for third-party software it used. true by default. PolymakeConfigPath
what to pass to polymake's --config-path. Empty, the default, makes polymake ignore all user configuration. Use "user" to honour ~/.polymake/settings instead; this is also considerably faster, as polymake then caches its autoconfiguration between calls. PolymakePreferences
a list of polymake rule preferences applied to every call, for example [ "*.convex_hull cdd" ] to choose a convex hull backend. Empty by default.
Everything polymake writes to standard error is captured. It is shown at level 2, and when a call fails it is part of the error message and of .
To see the current settings, use ShowUserPreferences("polymaking");. To change them for the current session:
SetUserPreference("polymaking", "PolymakeCommand", "/home/mypolymakebindir/polymake"); SetUserPreference("polymaking", "PolymakeDataDirectory", "/home/mypolymakedatadir");
Setting preferences permanently Add the two lines above to your gap.ini file, or call WriteGapIniFile(); once after setting them, and they will be used in every &GAP; session (see ). Unlike the global variables they replace, the preferences may be set at any time, also after LoadPackage("polymaking");.

If the preference is empty, a temporary directory is returned; it is created on demand and re-created if it has vanished, so this keeps working after loading a &GAP; workspace saved in an earlier session.
